length.text: Most adults about 35-82 cm; record 116 cm

activity.text: By day, in shrubs and trees

overview.text: The Rough Greensnake is a slender, bright green, harmless snake of the south-eastern and central United States. It lives in shrubs and low trees, often above water, and feeds almost entirely on insects and spiders.

identification.text: Very thin, with a long tail, plain bright green above and whitish or yellowish below. Its back scales are keeled (they have a ridge down the middle), which gives the "rough" in its name and separates it from the Smooth Greensnake.

size.label: Adults
size.text: Most adults are about 35-82 cm (14-33 in) in total length; the record is 116 cm. Some sources give ranges up to about 114 cm (45 in) for large adults.

distribution.label: Native
distribution.text: The south-eastern and south-central United States, from New Jersey to Florida and west to Kansas, Oklahoma and Texas, with records extending into north-eastern Mexico. SnakeList's map shows the states where it is recorded.

habitat.text: Dense vegetation - shrubs, vines and low trees - especially along the edges of streams, lakes and wetlands, where it often rests in branches overhanging water.

behaviour.text: Largely active by day and an excellent climber. Its green colour and habit of staying still among leaves make it hard to spot.

diet.text: Mostly insects and spiders: crickets, grasshoppers and caterpillars make up much of what it eats. Snails and small tree frogs are taken occasionally.

reproduction.text: Females lay eggs, usually about 3-12 per clutch (sources range from 1 to 14). Several females sometimes share a nest site, and up to 75 eggs have been found together in one such communal nest.

similar.text: the Smooth Greensnake of more northern and western areas, which has smooth, unkeeled scales and is generally smaller.

adw.title: Opheodrys aestivus (Rough Greensnake)
